title: stabilize tool_choice weighting and add compact v2 invoke envelope for OpenAI compatibility
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Stabilizes OpenAI-compatible tool_choice semantics by introducing deterministic weighted tie-break and introduces a compact v2 invoke envelope to reduce streaming fragmentation and improve schema-resilience. Includes telemetry for choice resolution and envelope emission. Backwards compatible with v1 envelopes.
description: Motivation: Several customer integrations hit nondeterministic tool selection when multiple tools had near-equal scores and streaming fragments from tool invocations produced noisy, reparsed payloads. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: (1) a deterministic, weight-aware tie-breaker for tool_choice decisions that combines explicit tool weight, provenance, and a seeded stable-hash to remove flakiness across retries; (2) an opt-in v2 invoke envelope for OpenAI-compatible streams that reduces per-fragment overhead, carries compact schema hints, and improves reassembly resilience under high-concurrency streaming. Summary of changes: Added ToolChoiceResolver that normalizes incoming OpenAI-style function/tool scores into a single selection score using configurable weight_decay and provenance_priority. The resolver exposes deterministic behavior via a stable seed derived from the request-id to ensure repeatable outcomes for retries and hedges. Introduced invoke_envelope v2: compact fragment header fields (env_id, frag_index, last_frag, frag_schema_crc, prov_ref) and a small delta encoding for repeated keys to reduce payload size. Implemented a v1->v2 compatibility adapter in the streaming decoder so hosted customers keep working while new clients opt-in. Telemetry and observability: emit tool_choice.resolve events with fields (chosen_tool, score_components, seed_hash, resolve_latency_ms) and new histograms for invoke.envelope_v2.emit.size_bytes and invoke.envelope_v2.reassembly.latency_ms. Tests: unit tests around deterministic tie-break across seeded retries, fuzz tests for fragmented v2 reassembly, integration tests covering OpenAI-compat adapter and fallback to v1. Also added a small canary job to perf-canary that runs 1000 short-stream invokes to measure regression. Backwards compatibility: v2 is opt-in; when the client sets header X-OpenAI-Envelope: v2 the runtime emits v2 fragments. Default remains v1. Rollout plan: start behind a feature flag for 48h on canary fleet, collect telemetry, then enable for 10% traffic before global rollout. See linked linear tickets for follow-ups on runtime autoscaling tweaks for v2 envelope.
commits_summary: 5 commits: introduce resolver and unit tests; add envelope v2 encoder/decoder; add telemetry and metrics; adapter for v1 compatibility and e2e tests; docs and changelog entry.
changed_paths_snippets: runtime/tool_choice/resolver.py: compute selection_score = normalized_score * exp(-weight_decay*rank) + provenance_boost
runtime/streaming/envelope_v2/encoder.py: emit header {env_id,frag_index,last_frag,frag_schema_crc,prov_ref} then compact payload bytes
runtime/streaming/adapter_v1_v2.py: decode v1 into v2-lite to permit downstream consumers to rely on consistent schema hints
telemetry/events/tool_choice.py: added emit('tool_choice.resolve', {chosen_tool, components, seed_hash, latency_ms})
review_thread: Arjun Patel: Please add an explicit seed derivation function in resolver so behavior is auditable. Also add unit test for retry determinism.
Maya Chen: added derive_seed(request_id, client_ts) helper and unit test; test added in test_tool_choice_resolver.py (commit 3)
Lena Kovacs: Can you clarify how provenance_boost interacts with explicit tool weight? Edge case where a low-weight tool has provenance_high must not always win.
Maya Chen: adjusted algorithm to cap provenance_boost to a configurable max_provenance_boost and documented expected behavior in docs/openai_compat.md
Diego Flores: CI flake observed in e2e reassembly test; looks like timing assumptions in test. Recommend switching to event-driven wait for 'reassembly_complete' telemetry in the test.
Maya Chen: switched e2e test to poll telemetry event; CI passed on rerun. Approving review.
ci_checks: perf-smoke: pass (envelope v2 shows ~12% payload reduction for short fragments)
notes_for_ops: Feature flag 'openai.envelope_v2' added. Add 'envelope_v2' pod annotation to dedicated clusters during staged rollout. Watch telemetry: tool_choice.resolve.error_rate and invoke.envelope_v2.reassembly.failure_count before increasing traffic.
docs_changes: docs/openai_compat.md: new section 'Envelope v2' with examples and migration steps; sdk/openai_compat_adapter.md: added code snippets showing header usage and fallback behavior.
manual_backports: None required. Backwards compatible; no customer migrations needed other than opt-in header.
qa_notes: Manual QA: validated usage with Python SDK adapter and raw cURL header; validated deterministic selection across retries by replaying same request-id. Added e2e telemetry assertions in CI.
known_issues: v2 reassembly relies on frag_schema_crc present; in some legacy clients the schema may be absent which will trigger v1 fallback; telemetry emits invoke.envelope_v2.fallback_count in that case.
